subject: giant bird soaring
title: What If the Heaviest Flying Bird Ever Were Alive? It Weighed as Much as a Man

scenes.text: What if the heaviest bird that ever flew were alive? It weighed as much as a man.
scenes.keywords: giant bird silhouette sky adult man

scenes.text: Argentavis soared over Argentina six million years ago: about 70 kilograms, with wings spanning seven metres.
Today's widest wings, the wandering albatross, reach 3.5 metres. The Andean condor weighs around 15 kilos.
A 2007 study found flapping would need 600 watts of power. Its muscles could manage about 170.
So it ran downhill into a headwind to get airborne, then rode thermals at around 67 kilometres per hour.
A 2014 fossil, Pelagornis, may have had wider wings, but at under 40 kilos. On weight, Argentavis still rules the sky.

description:
What if the heaviest flying bird ever were alive today? Argentavis magnificens lived in Argentina about six million years ago, weighed roughly 70 kilograms and had a wingspan of about seven metres.
A 2007 PNAS study calculated that sustained flapping needed around 600 watts against about 170 available, so it launched from slopes into headwinds and soared on thermals at about 67 km/h. Pelagornis sandersi (2014) may have had a wider wingspan but weighed under 40 kg.
